errorMap.notes: A ChatGPT plan has usage windows, not credit: a 429 usage_limit_reached is the plan's 5-hour or weekly window (x-codex-primary-* and x-codex-secondary-* headers carry used-percent and reset-after-seconds). A 401 (detail: 'Could not parse your authentication token') is an access token that's gone: oauth_expired.

privacy.retention: ChatGPT's own, as set in the player's ChatGPT data controls; store:false sent
privacy.trains: Per the player's ChatGPT setting (Improve the model for everyone)
privacy.notes: Requests run under the player's ChatGPT account and plan, as Codex's do; the ChatGPT Terms of Use and the account's data controls apply.

player.short: Follows your ChatGPT data controls; uses your plan’s limits.
player.keeps: What ChatGPT keeps for your account. You can check it in ChatGPT’s data controls.
player.trains: Only if Improve the model for everyone is on in your ChatGPT settings.
player.sets: Asks OpenAI not to store the replies.

terms.login: Sign in with ChatGPT (OAuth with PKCE, Codex's public client id). OpenAI supports ChatGPT-plan sign-in in third-party tools; usage counts against the plan's Codex limits.
notes: The access token stays in memory; the key store keeps the account id and refresh token only.
The Codex backend needs the chatgpt-account-id header and a client_version on its model list.
playerNotes: Uses your ChatGPT plan instead of an API key, with no charge per reply.
Replies count toward your plan’s usage limits, which reset every few hours.
